"executive_summary": "This paper establishes that the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the coherent cohomology of any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme of a mod p abelian type compact Shimura variety at hyperspecial level coincide with those appearing in the cohomology of the Shimura variety itself. The author extends earlier results that were restricted to smooth zero-dimensional subschemes to higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes. The central mechanism is a refined going-down argument that reduces an arbitrary subscheme to a smooth closed subscheme admitting a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section, thereby enabling the use of Hasse invariants. Analogous results are proven for nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties, including Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. The work builds on the foundational framework of Goldring-Koskivirta and Terakado-Yu, generalizing their techniques while overcoming the obstructions posed by singularities and higher dimensionality. The results have implications for the study of Hecke modules and the structure of mod p Shimura varieties.",

"executive_summary": "This paper establishes a uniform principle for the mod p fiber of abelian-type Shimura varieties at hyperspecial level: the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in coherent cohomology with coefficients in automorphic line bundles are identical whether computed on the whole special fiber or on any Hecke-equivariant subscheme. The central object is the special fiber SK of the Kisin-Vasiu integral canonical model of a Shimura variety of abelian type at good reduction, equipped with the prime-to-p Hecke action. Prior work by Goldring-Koskivirta and by Terakado-Yu proved analogous equalities but only for subschemes that are smooth of dimension 0, such as the zero-dimensional Ekedahl-Oort stratum or zero-dimensional central leaves. The present work generalizes these results to higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes, and to nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties. The main theorem (Theorem A) states that for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme YK of SK, the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the direct sums of H0 over the L-dominant characters eta of the automorphic line bundles V(eta) are the same on SK and on YK. The proof introduces a novel three-step strategy: a refined going-down argument, a new further going-down argument, and the unchanged going-up argument of the prior literature. The refined going-down argument relates Hecke eigenforms on the Shimura variety to Hecke eigenforms of the sheaf of differentials via the conormal exact sequence, building on Ghitza. The new further going-down argument is the key innovation: because higher-dimensional and singular subschemes lack a nowhere vanishing Hecke-invariant section and have a conormal sequence that is neither exact nor locally free, the author intersects the subscheme with the smallest length stratum it meets nontrivially and successively removes nonsingular points to obtain a smooth closed subscheme ZK that admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. This step crucially uses the existence of Hasse invariants, in contrast to the going-down argument of the prior literature. The going-up argument of the prior literature then applies verbatim to relate eigenvalues on ZK to YK and SK. The results apply in particular to the closures of Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, Newton strata, and central leaves, including higher-dimensional central leaves. The paper also treats nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties, requiring Hodge type or properness in some cases, and provides a corollary for Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. The framework relies on G-zip theory, automorphic vector bundles, and the theory of Hasse invariants, and it extends to toroidal compactifications under an ampleness assumption. The work is purely theoretical with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code, and it contributes a conceptual unification rather than empirical findings.",

summary.title: Systems of Hecke eigenvalues on subschemes of Shimura varieties
summary.field_subfield: Number theory / arithmetic geometry (Shimura varieties, mod p cohomology)
summary.executive_summary: This paper establishes a uniform principle for the mod p fiber of abelian-type Shimura varieties at hyperspecial level: the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in coherent cohomology with coefficients in automorphic line bundles are identical whether computed on the whole special fiber or on any Hecke-equivariant subscheme. The central object is the special fiber SK of the Kisin-Vasiu integral canonical model of a Shimura variety of abelian type at good reduction, equipped with the prime-to-p Hecke action. Prior work by Goldring-Koskivirta and by Terakado-Yu proved analogous equalities but only for subschemes that are smooth of dimension 0, such as the zero-dimensional Ekedahl-Oort stratum or zero-dimensional central leaves. The present work generalizes these results to higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes, and to nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties. The main theorem (Theorem A) states that for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme YK of SK, the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the direct sums of H0 over the L-dominant characters eta of the automorphic line bundles V(eta) are the same on SK and on YK. The proof introduces a novel three-step strategy: a refined going-down argument, a new further going-down argument, and the unchanged going-up argument of the prior literature. The refined going-down argument relates Hecke eigenforms on the Shimura variety to Hecke eigenforms of the sheaf of differentials via the conormal exact sequence, building on Ghitza. The new further going-down argument is the key innovation: because higher-dimensional and singular subschemes lack a nowhere vanishing Hecke-invariant section and have a conormal sequence that is neither exact nor locally free, the author intersects the subscheme with the smallest length stratum it meets nontrivially and successively removes nonsingular points to obtain a smooth closed subscheme ZK that admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. This step crucially uses the existence of Hasse invariants, in contrast to the going-down argument of the prior literature. The going-up argument of the prior literature then applies verbatim to relate eigenvalues on ZK to YK and SK. The results apply in particular to the closures of Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, Newton strata, and central leaves, including higher-dimensional central leaves. The paper also treats nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties, requiring Hodge type or properness in some cases, and provides a corollary for Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. The framework relies on G-zip theory, automorphic vector bundles, and the theory of Hasse invariants, and it extends to toroidal compactifications under an ampleness assumption. The work is purely theoretical with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code, and it contributes a conceptual unification rather than empirical findings.

claims.description: The systems of Hecke eigenvalues on the special fiber SK equal those on any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme.
The further going-down argument constructs a smooth closed subscheme ZK admitting a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section.
The result extends to nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties under conditions.

Executive Summary
This paper establishes a uniform principle for the mod p fiber of abelian-type Shimura varieties at hyperspecial level: the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in coherent cohomology with coefficients in automorphic line bundles are identical whether computed on the whole special fiber or on any Hecke-equivariant subscheme. The central object is the special fiber SK of the Kisin-Vasiu integral canonical model of a Shimura variety of abelian type at good reduction, equipped with the prime-to-p Hecke action. Prior work by Goldring-Koskivirta and by Terakado-Yu proved analogous equalities but only for subschemes that are smooth of dimension 0, such as the zero-dimensional Ekedahl-Oort stratum or zero-dimensional central leaves. The present work generalizes these results to higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes, and to nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties. The main theorem (Theorem A) states that for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme YK of SK, the systems of Hecke eigenvalues appearing in the direct sums of H0 over the L-dominant characters eta of the automorphic line bundles V(eta) are the same on SK and on YK. The proof introduces a novel three-step strategy: a refined going-down argument, a new further going-down argument, and the unchanged going-up argument of the prior literature. The refined going-down argument relates Hecke eigenforms on the Shimura variety to Hecke eigenforms of the sheaf of differentials via the conormal exact sequence, building on Ghitza. The new further going-down argument is the key innovation: because higher-dimensional and singular subschemes lack a nowhere vanishing Hecke-invariant section and have a conormal sequence that is neither exact nor locally free, the author intersects the subscheme with the smallest length stratum it meets nontrivially and successively removes nonsingular points to obtain a smooth closed subscheme ZK that admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. This step crucially uses the existence of Hasse invariants, in contrast to the going-down argument of the prior literature. The going-up argument of the prior literature then applies verbatim to relate eigenvalues on ZK to YK and SK. The results apply in particular to the closures of Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, Newton strata, and central leaves, including higher-dimensional central leaves. The paper also treats nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties, requiring Hodge type or properness in some cases, and provides a corollary for Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. The framework relies on G-zip theory, automorphic vector bundles, and the theory of Hasse invariants, and it extends to toroidal compactifications under an ampleness assumption. The work is purely theoretical with no numerical experiments, datasets, or code, and it contributes a conceptual unification rather than empirical findings.

Research Context
The mod p fiber of an abelian type Shimura variety at good reduction carries a prime-to-p Hecke action. Several well-studied subschemes are invariant under this Hecke action. Serre's letter to Tate relates eigenvalues on a modular curve to those on the supersingular locus. Goldring-Koskivirta generalized this to Hodge-type Shimura varieties via the Kisin-Vasiu integral model. Terakado-Yu extended the method to central leaves in the basic Newton stratum. The prior results are restricted to subschemes that are smooth of dimension 0. The gap is the absence of results for higher-dimensional and possibly singular subschemes.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether Hecke eigenvalues on the whole special fiber match those on arbitrary subschemes. The hypothesis is that the equality holds for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme, not just smooth zero-dimensional ones. The predicted outcome is that eigenvalues coincide across the full range of subschemes, including higher-dimensional and singular ones. The expected mechanism is a refined going-down argument combined with a new further going-down argument. The anticipated tool is the existence of Hasse invariants on the constructed smooth subscheme. The going-up direction is expected to reuse the prior literature's argument verbatim. The corollary predicts equality for Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves.

Methodological Details
The setting is the special fiber of the Kisin-Vasiu integral canonical model of an abelian type Shimura variety. The level is hyperspecial, with K equal to Kp times Kp. The prime p is fixed as not equal to 2, over which G is unramified. The group is assumed to be the cuspidal quotient Gc, split over the reals but anisotropic over the rationals. The Hecke algebra has Zp coefficients and is prime-to-p. The Hecke algebra is the restricted tensor product over ramified places and p. G-zips are modeled as a smooth algebraic kappa-stack of dimension 0 isomorphic to a quotient stack. The Levi subgroup L is the centralizer of the Hodge cocharacter mu. Automorphic vector bundles arise from representations of P into the general linear group. The Hodge line bundle is the determinant of the sheaf of differentials. The L-dominant characters index the automorphic line bundles V(eta). The Ekedahl-Oort stratification is indexed by minimal length representatives of the Weyl group cosets. The length strata are indexed by the length function into the natural numbers. The Hasse invariants are sections whose nonvanishing locus is exactly the stratum. The central leaf is defined via an isomorphism of Dieudonne modules. The cohomology modules are direct sums over the L-dominant characters. The relation of eigenvalue systems is denoted with arrows and a double arrow for equality. The Hecke action is defined by push-pull on global sections. The Hecke-equivariant systems include strata, Newton strata, and central leaves.

Procedures And Architectures
The refined going-down argument relates Hecke eigenforms to the sheaf of differentials via the conormal exact sequence. The new further going-down argument constructs a smooth closed subscheme ZK from the given subscheme. The constructed subscheme admits a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. The transition from the ideal sheaf in YK to the ideal sheaf in SK is a key step. The going-up argument relates eigenvalues on ZK to YK and SK. The inductive construction defines a decreasing chain of closed subschemes. The minimality of the chain is guaranteed by the Noetherian property. Smoothness of the final subscheme is established by contradiction. The nowhere vanishing section is verified using the smallest length stratum. The injectivity of the section follows from the reduced structure. The main theorem concludes with a double arrow between the eigenvalue systems. The corollary extends the result to Ekedahl-Oort strata, length strata, and central leaves. The noncompact case requires Hodge type or properness. The toroidal compactification extends the morphism and Hecke action. The ampleness assumption ensures equality with the compactification.

Key Results
Theorem A states equality of Hecke eigenvalues for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. The equality holds between the cohomology of SK and the cohomology of YK. Theorem A applies to the closure of all subschemes mentioned in the introduction. Theorem A applies to higher-dimensional central leaves. Theorem B covers Ekedahl-Oort strata and length strata. Theorem B covers central leaves under properness conditions. The corollary establishes equality for strata and central leaves. The refined going-down argument uses Serre vanishing and the conormal sequence. The injection of Hecke modules is established via the conormal exact sequence. The going-up argument reuses the prior literature's lemma verbatim. The nonclosed subscheme result provides a one-directional implication. The closed subscheme result provides the reverse implication. Meeting the basic locus yields full equality. The nonvanishing locus of a Hecke-equivariant section yields equality. The extension to the compactification is established under the ampleness assumption.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The main implication is a uniform principle across all Hecke-equivariant subschemes. The equality unifies the eigenvalues on the whole variety and its subschemes. The Hasse invariants are essential to the going-down argument. The further going-down argument overcomes the singular and higher-dimensional obstructions. The construction of ZK resolves the obstruction to a nowhere vanishing section. The result generalizes the prior literature's zero-dimensional setting. The framework applies to a broad class of subschemes and strata. The noncompact case extends the theory beyond compact Shimura varieties. The ampleness assumption enables the toroidal compactification extension. The result connects to the theory of Serre's letter to Tate.

Contradictions And Limitations
The technical assumption G = Gc restricts the generality of the results. The assumption is needed for the abelian type case but not used elsewhere. The noncompact case requires Hodge type or properness. The toroidal compactification requires an ampleness assumption. The theory of toroidal compactifications of abelian type Shimura varieties is not yet developed. The paper omits discussion on compactifications for brevity. The dimension of central leaves is described combinatorially but omitted here.

Claims
The systems of Hecke eigenvalues on the special fiber SK equal those on any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. Theorem A establishes the equality for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. The equality is expressed via the double arrow relation. The result holds via the refined and further going-down arguments. The technical assumption G = Gc restricts the generality. The noncompact case requires Hodge type or properness. The result unifies the eigenvalues across the whole variety and its subschemes. The result generalizes the prior literature's zero-dimensional setting.
The further going-down argument constructs a smooth closed subscheme ZK admitting a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. The construction intersects with the smallest length stratum. The construction removes nonsingular points of the intersection. The resulting subscheme is smooth and closed. The subscheme admits a nowhere vanishing section. The original subscheme lacks a nowhere vanishing section. The conormal sequence is not exact or locally free. The construction resolves the obstructions to the going-down argument. The Hasse invariants are essential to the argument.
The result extends to nonclosed subschemes and noncompact Shimura varieties under conditions. The nonclosed subscheme result provides a one-directional implication. The closed subscheme result provides the reverse implication. Meeting the basic locus yields full equality. The noncompact case requires Hodge type or properness. The toroidal compactification requires an ampleness assumption. The theory of toroidal compactifications of abelian type Shimura varieties is not yet developed. The result broadens the theory beyond compact Shimura varieties. The ampleness assumption enables the toroidal compactification extension.

Data And Code Availability
The paper is purely theoretical with no data or code.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The result holds for any Hecke-equivariant closed subscheme. The result holds for Ekedahl-Oort strata and length strata. The result holds for central leaves under properness conditions. The result holds for nonclosed subschemes. The result holds for noncompact Shimura varieties. The result holds under the ampleness assumption for the compactification.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a uniform principle for Hecke eigenvalues across all Hecke-equivariant subschemes. 2. The strongest evidence is the construction of a smooth closed subscheme ZK admitting a nowhere vanishing Hecke-equivariant section. 3. The future path is the development of the theory of toroidal compactifications of abelian type Shimura varieties.
